column3: NASB follows the critical text; “having in womb” is rendered “was with child,” and the present “cries out” is rendered as past.
“Drags” is rendered “swept away”; NASB renders the presents as past.
NASB follows the critical text (“a son, a male child”).
NASB follows the critical text; “they may feed her” is rendered “she might be nourished.”
NASB follows the critical text (“waging war with the dragon”).
NASB follows the critical text (“they were not strong enough”).
“Ancient” is rendered “of old,” and “the inhabited world” “the whole world.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the accuser … has been thrown down”); “brothers” is rendered “brethren.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Woe to the earth and the sea”); “fury” is rendered “wrath,” and NASB adds “only.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the two wings”); “face” is rendered “presence.”
NASB follows the critical text; “cast” is rendered “poured.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the testimony of Jesus,” without “Christ”); “children” is rendered “offspring.”
NASB has no separate verse 18; its words (“And he stood on the sand of the seashore”) begin NASB’s 13:1, following the critical text (“he stood”).
